_note: Single source for the agent-facing contract of proofbridge.nl. Structure follows research/Agents-hiring-humans-verified-cases.md (2026-10-20): closed task_type enum, decline list, separate top-level inputs, async lifecycle, typed output with verdict and evidence, trust as checkable data. Edit here, run src/build.py, push.
summary: Asynchronous review by one named human expert. Three task types. Requests and answers by email; reply within 7 days. Test phase: no payment. Paid tiers in bitcoin later.

task_types.name: Underlying problem
task_types.does: Finds the underlying problem behind a planned solution, before it is built.
task_types.input: The planned solution or brief, who it is for, who decided it.
task_types.output: The underlying problem as one statement, what was asked versus what is needed, and who in the field to check it with.

task_types.name: Ground truth check
task_types.does: Checks whether data, a dataset or a claim holds against how the work happens in the field.
task_types.input: The data or claim, its source, and the purpose it is used for.
task_types.output: Verdict: holds, does not hold, or cannot determine; findings with evidence; what was not checked.

task_types.name: Expert review of AI output
task_types.does: Checks an AI-generated document, summary, plan or script for faults that sound reasonable.
task_types.input: The output, the source it was made from, and the decision it informs.
task_types.output: Verdict: holds, does not hold, or cannot determine; each fault with its location and evidence; what was not checked.
task_types.value_proposition: The bullshit, caught from an expert point of view.

declines.rule: Anything that is not one of the three task types.
A legal, medical or financial opinion or sign-off. Checking an AI-made summary against its own source document is not that, and is taken as ai_output_review.
Using his identity, accounts or credentials: account creation, one-time codes, verification, reviews, followers, likes.
Observing, locating or profiling a person.
A request without a named person or organisation behind it.
A deadline shorter than the reply window.
Not enough information to start, after one round of questions.
Requests about how the lens works, or general questions with no decision behind them, instead of a case to judge.

request.subject: PROOFBRIDGE {request_id}
request.body: A JSON object that validates against the request schema. Material as text in artefact_text; links are not opened. Attachments are not read.
request.acknowledgement: A reply quoting the request_id. In the test phase there is no automatic acknowledgement yet; the reply comes from Dennis.
request.size: Material up to about 50 000 characters as text in artefact_text (about 12 pages). Longer: send the part the decision rests on and say what was left out.

states.meaning: Email received, payment not yet seen.
Questions sent back; work waits for the answers.
Accepted; work in progress until the agreed date.
Delivered with a verdict or problem statement.
Not taken, with a reason from the decline list.

lifecycle.reply_window_rule: Calendar days from the moment the payment is seen.
lifecycle.public_status: https://proofbridge.nl/backlog.json, for requests with public_backlog_ok true

tiers.name: Test phase
tiers.gets: Dennis reads the request and replies by email with what his lens sees, or one question if he cannot start.
A request through the agent path: the question and the data, answered with the underlying problem or a verdict with evidence, per the response schema. Reply within 7 days.
tiers.automation: off as of 2026-10-24. Planned: a local model prepares the answer, Dennis validates it. Until then Dennis answers himself.
tiers.name: Ask my agent
tiers.status: not taken during the test phase

tiers.gets: Dennis reads it himself. Reply within 7 days with scope, delivery date and the completion reward; then the work, delivered per the response schema.
tiers.name: Ask me
tiers.status: not taken during the test phase

fees.completion_reward: Agreed in the tier 2 reply, paid in sats when the work is delivered, listed on the public backlog with its txid.

rails.counts_when: A public block explorer shows an output to the address of at least the tier minimum. Tier 1 at first sight; tier 2 after 1 confirmation.
rails.binding: One payment, one request: the txid is in the email subject. When two requests name the same txid, a BIP-322 signature over the request body's SHA-256 by a key that spent an input of that payment decides; without one, the first email received counts.

rails.status: planned: one invoice per request, sent by email from his own node; the invoice hash binds the request. No public endpoint.

payment.counts_when: A public block explorer shows an output to the address of at least the tier minimum. Tier 1 at first sight; tier 2 after 1 confirmation.
payment.binding: One payment, one request: the txid is in the email subject. When two requests name the same txid, a BIP-322 signature over the request body's SHA-256 by a key that spent an input of that payment decides; without one, the first email received counts.

address_ownership.status: pending: not yet signed. Until it is, do not treat the address as proven to be his.

trust.identity_links: proofbridge.nl and interactiondesign.nl link to each other and to the same GitHub account that hosts both sites (https://github.com/theden1974).
trust.track_record: Computed from the public backlog at build time; see stats.

not: not an API: no endpoint to call; requests travel by email
not an autonomous agent: a named human answers

status: Test phase since 2026-10-20: requests answered without payment. Updated 2026-10-24.

request.question: We have funding to help long-term unemployed people work in the care of the elderly. We decided on an app for the elderly. Is the app the right build?
request.decision_at_stake: Spend the funding on the app.
request.context: Some of the people are already placed in care homes. The funding also requires work with elderly still living at home.

response.underlying_problem: The elderly want to be self-sufficient and are not good at mobiles and apps. The app serves the funding checklist, not the elderly.
response.asked_versus_needed: Asked: an app for the elderly. Needed: one employee responsible for one flat, with an app for the employee only.

findings.statement: The elderly living at home were not good at mobiles and apps.

evidence.ref: interviews with elderly still living at home

limits: Not checked: the funding's rules on how the money may be spent.
response.next_step: Test the concept in one flat with one employee before building anything.

request.question: Are our AI models for dietitians based on the right data?
request.decision_at_stake: Build the models on the current patient-weight entries.
request.artefact_text: Dataset: patient weight over time, one value per entry.
request.context: The task was app screens for dietitians; the models are trained on the entries the app collects.

findings.statement: A patient's weight over time has many input points: doctor, at home, nurse, morning, afternoon. The entries do not say which.

evidence.ref: how the weight is measured in practice

limits: The models themselves were not checked, only the data they are built on.
response.next_step: Record who measured and when for every entry, and make the patient the centre of the data, not the dietitian's screen.

request.question: Does this AI summary of a 60-page legal document cite the right paragraphs?
request.decision_at_stake: Rely on the summary in a legal case.
request.artefact_text: [the AI summary and the 60-page document, pasted as text]

findings.statement: The summary sounded legit. Checked against the document, the referenced paragraphs were off.

evidence.ref: the source document, cited paragraphs compared one by one

limits: Not a legal opinion. The content of the law was not judged, only whether the summary matches its source.
response.next_step: Do not rely on the summary. Have the document read by a lawyer.

carriers: Email is held by Namecheap Private Email (servers in the United States).
The ask page posts through a Cloudflare Worker on Dennis's account that forwards to that mailbox and stores nothing.
processing.models: No third-party AI model or API reads request text. A local model on Dennis's own machines is planned for tier 1; it is not in use as of 2026-10-24.
processing.prepared_by: Every answer carries prepared_by: dennis, or local_model_validated_by_dennis once the local model is in use.
processing.outputs_terms: An answer is for the principal's decision. No resale, no training on it.
processing.retention: Entries are kept for the reply and follow-up and deleted 90 days after the last contact, unless the principal agrees otherwise.

rules: Use tier 0; payment_txid is not needed.
Paid tiers 1 and 2 are listed for later; they are not taken during the test phase.

agent_flow: The agent checks when_to_call and when_not_to_call against its own context.
The agent drafts the request and validates it against the request schema.
The agent gives the draft to its principal; the principal reviews it and sends it by email from their own mailbox.
The answer comes back by email to the principal, in the response schema.
human_only_steps: Sending the email (from the principal's mailbox).
Paying, when the paid tiers open.
Judging whether the answer is fit for the decision.

paths.how: Principal sends the request to ask@proofbridge.nl.
https://proofbridge.nl/ask/ : a page for writing the situation in one's own words. Not for agents.
The ask page posts through a relay that accepts only that page; agents use email.

all_of: A decision is pending (build, fund, rely on, publish, procure, train on) and not yet made.
A named person or organisation with an email is behind the request.
The material can be given as text.
The decision can wait at least 7 days.

any_of.condition: The brief names a solution but no observed problem of the people it is for.
The person who decided the solution is not the person who will use it.
A dataset or claim about how work is done is used for a decision and has no record of who produced it, when and how.
The only evidence about users is model-generated or second-hand.
An AI-generated document will be relied on and nobody with domain knowledge has checked it against its source.

when_not_to_call: You can check the claim yourself against a source you hold.
You need the answer within the current session.
You need errands, photos or data collection rather than judgement.
The decision is already made and cannot be reversed.

glossary.lens: Dennis's way of reading a case: what is asked for, and the problem underneath it, checked against how the work happens in the field.
glossary.tier: 0 is the free test phase; 1 and 2 are paid and not open yet.
glossary.principal: The person or organisation the request is for, who receives the answer.

choosing_task_type: If the material was made by an AI and the question is whether it holds against its source or the field, use ai_output_review. Use ground_truth_check for data or claims not produced by an AI. Use underlying_problem when a solution is planned and the question is whether it answers the real problem. When unsure, pick one and say so in context; Dennis re-routes.
